# Performance comparison with PDFium and pdf.js

<!-- Generated by bench/perf-report.sh (tools/PerfCompare). Do not edit by hand: run the script again. -->

How fast Broadside opens, renders and extracts text from real-world PDFs, next to PDFium (the engine in Chrome) and pdf.js
(the engine in Firefox), and how much memory each needs. Ratios are Broadside's time divided by the other engine's: below 1
means Broadside is faster.

## How it is measured

- **Pages.** The 21 pinned pages of the rendering gate (`tests/Broadside.Rendering.Tests/CorpusGate/pinned-pages.txt`), from 20
  files of the pdf.js, Ghent Workgroup and PDF Association test suites. They were picked to cover features (blend modes, spot
  colors, every image format, shadings, patterns, soft masks, embedded fonts), not for speed.
- **Engines.** Broadside with its software rasterizer on .NET; PDFium through pypdfium2; pdf.js in Node with its in-process
  worker and `@napi-rs/canvas`. Each runs in its own process with the same protocol (`tools/PerfCompare`,
  `tools/RenderDiff/reference/pdfium/bench.py`, `tools/RenderDiff/reference/pdfjs/bench.mjs`).
- **Protocol.** Before anything is timed, every page runs twice untimed, so that code compiled at run time (.NET, V8) is
  fully optimized for the first file as for the last. Then each case warms up untimed for 0.5 s or 20 runs, whichever
  comes first, and is timed for up to the configured number of runs (at least 3, fewer once a case has used 10 s). Times
  are medians. Everything runs on one thread.
- **Fonts.** Broadside uses its bundled Standard 14 fonts and CMaps and no system fonts; the others use their own bundled fonts.
- **Cold and warm.** *First render* and *whole document* open a fresh copy of the file each run, so nothing from an earlier
  run is reused. *Render* and *extract text* reuse an open document, as a viewer does when it redraws a page. The process
  itself is always warm (code compiled, files in the OS cache).
- **Memory.** A fresh process per engine and file opens the file, renders every page at 150 DPI and extracts its text,
  then reports its peak resident set size. The table shows the peak minus the same process with the engine loaded and
  nothing opened, so each runtime's own size (Python, Node, .NET) is left out.
- **Browser.** Broadside's Blazor WebAssembly demo (AOT build, software rasterizer, main thread) and pdf.js (its Web
  Worker and a canvas) time the same pages in the same headless Chromium, on a cross-origin isolated page so the clock is
  precise. pdf.js renders with its print intent: its display intent waits for an animation frame, which adds about 8 ms to
  every render whatever the page holds. The two intents differ only for content hidden when printing. After each render pdf.js
  reads one pixel back from its canvas, which waits for the GPU to finish drawing, so both times include the pixels.

| Operation | What is timed |
|---|---|
| Open | Open the file from memory and read the page's size. |
| Extract text | On an open document, extract the page's text. |
| Render | On an open document, render the page again (fonts and images already loaded, the page's content read again). |
| First render | Open the file and render the page: what a viewer pays to show it the first time. |
| Whole document | Open the file and render every page. |

Shared machines and CI runners are noisy: expect 10 to 30% between runs, more on pages that take under a millisecond.
Results below: GitHub-hosted Linux runner (ubuntu-24.04), GitHub-hosted macOS runner (macos-latest), macOS 27, Apple M4 Max (a developer machine).

### Summary

Geometric mean of the per-page ratios, and the slowest page relative to the other engine.

| Open |  | 21 | 0.05x | 0.2x | 0.07x | 0.5x |
| Extract text |  | 21 | 0.21x | 0.8x | 0.04x | 0.2x |
| Render | 72 | 21 | 0.54x | 2.6x | 0.21x | 0.6x |
| Render | 150 | 21 | 0.51x | 3.2x | 0.33x | 1.3x |
| First render | 72 | 21 | 0.66x | 2.0x | 0.23x | 0.5x |

### Targets

The targets proposed with the Phase 3 baseline (issue #140). A missed target blocks 1.0 unless the owner accepts it in writing.

| Target | Measured | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Render at 72 DPI: at most 1.0x PDFium on average, no page over 3x | 0.54x, slowest 2.6x | met |
| Render at 150 DPI: at most 1.0x PDFium on average, no page over 3x | 0.51x, slowest 3.2x | **missed** |
| First render at 72 DPI: at most 1.25x PDFium on average, no page over 4x | 0.66x, slowest 2.0x | met |
| First render at 150 DPI: at most 1.25x PDFium on average, no page over 4x | 0.60x, slowest 1.6x | met |
| Never slower than pdf.js (Node) on any page and operation | 2 slower: pdfjs/alphatrans.pdf render 150 (1.34x); pdfjs/issue6296.pdf render 150 (1.06x) | **missed** |
| Open: under 0.25x PDFium on average | 0.05x | met |
| Extract text: under 0.5x PDFium on average | 0.21x | met |
| Render at 72 DPI allocates at most 1 MB per page | largest 745 KB | met |
